title: Lifting a computation before an exit state
statement: Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,S'$ be state sets, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $M$ and $H$ be deterministic Turing machines with $k$ and $k+l$ work tapes, respectively. Fix a map $e:S\to S'$, an exit state $q_{\mathrm{exit}}\in S$, a starting configuration $c$ of $M$, and contents and head positions for the additional $l$ tapes. Suppose that at every state $q\ne q_{\mathrm{exit}}$, for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ at state $e(q)$ is the action of $M$ on its first $k$ tapes, extended by leaving the additional tapes unchanged and mapping the successor state by $e$. If the run of $M$ from $c$ is not in state $q_{\mathrm{exit}}$ at any time $j<t$, then at every time $j\le t$, the run of $H$ from the configuration formed by embedding $c$ via $e$ and adjoining the chosen additional tapes equals the embedded configuration of $M$ at time $j$.
hypotheses_covered: Transition agreement at every non-exit state, for every input symbol and work-tape tuple
Contents and head positions for the additional $l$ tapes
The run of $M$ is not in the exit state at any time $j<t$
replaced: Suppose a host machine agrees, on every embedded non-exit control, with the disjoint-bank lift of a smaller machine acting on the left tapes. Then for every start configuration of the smaller machine, every retained right-bank contents and heads, and every horizon $t$ such that the smaller machine does not reach the exit control before $t$, the host run agrees with the lifted run of the smaller machine at every time up to $t$. No agreement is required after the first exit.
